 ‘3 Body Problem’ Sets Season 2 Release Date at Netflix (TV News Roundup)
 By 
 Isabelle Farina , Mya Copeland 
 Add us as a Google Preferred Source
 ED MILLER/NETFLIX 
 Comments 
 Netflix’s sci-fi thriller “ 3 Body Problem ” returns for Season 2 on Jan. 14.
 The series, based on the popular “Remembrance of Earth’s Past” book series by Chinese author Liu Cixin, explores complex questions about the nature of the universe, leading a group of scientists to partner with a detective to confront an existential planetary threat in the wake of the Chinese Cultural Revolution in the 1960s.
 Related Stories 
 Skydance Movie Studio Shakeup: Kira Goldberg Departs Netflix to Run Paramount With Don Granger, Jeff Goldstein to Retire, WB Sets Leadership 
 James Gunn Says 'No One From Skydance' Has Seen 'Superman' Sequel 'Man of Tomorrow' as Rumors Fly After His DC Studios Exit 
 In Season 2, “the alien invasion nears and humanity prepares to meet them — on Earth and beyond. While a space fleet embarks on a mission that spans centuries, a secret locked inside of one man’s mind might be humanity’s only hope for survival.”
 The trailer and teaser images give a first look at this season’s otherworldly forces as the alien invasion nears. Some are devout San-Ti followers, like Tatiana (Marlo Kelly), and will stop at nothing to help the alien agenda. 
 Returning alongside Kelly are Jovan Adepo as Saul Durand, Liam Cunningham as Thomas Wade, Eiza González as Auggie Salazar, Jess Hong as Jin Cheng, Benedict Wong as Da Shi, Sea Shimooka as Sophon and Saamer Usmani as Raj Varma. New recruits also join the human forces in Season 2, with Claudia Doumit (“SOULM8TE,” “The Boys”) joining the cast as Captain Van Rijn and Ellie de Lange (“Run Away,” “Wolf Hall,” “The Serpent”) as Ayla.
 The series is created and executive produced by David Benioff and D.B. Weiss (“Game of Thrones”) and Alexander Woo (“True Blood,” “The Terror”). The first season was released in 2024.

 Development/Production 
 Masterpiece PBS has announced a new period crime drama “Fleet Street” from the creators of “Miss Scarlet,” Rachael New and Ben Edwards.
 Set in 1901 London, the death of a local florist tied to the royals captures the attention of aspiring journalist Kitty Parker (Silvia Presente) and The Morning Herald reporter Samuel Wallace (Guy Remmers), giving the duo their first lead. A missing son, anonymous messages and a gruesome death send them on an investigation that could shape their careers or put them in imminent danger.
 Filming for the six-part first season will begin in December, and the series will launch in the U.K. on UKTV’s free streaming service U and air on U&Drama. “Fleet Street” is co-produced by Mikey Productions Limited and Masterpiece. Executive producing are New, Edwards, Patricia Lenahan and Patrick Irwin for Mikey Productions Limited. Susanne Simpson is the executive producer for Masterpiece, and Claire Hookway and Karin Marelle are the executive producers for UKTV. Ivan Živković serves as lead director.
 First Looks/Trailers 
 “My Next Guest Needs No Introduction with David Letterman” returns for its seventh season Dec. 15 on Netflix, with a new trailer available now.
 The forthcoming season of the Emmy Award-winning series features conversations with actors Matt Damon and Julia Roberts, late-night host Jimmy Kimmel and professional climber Alex Honnold. Previous guests include Barack Obama, Tina Fey, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, JAY-Z, Robert Downey Jr., Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Dave Chappelle, Michael B. Jordan, Miley Cyrus, Caitlin Clark, Billie Eilish and Adam Sandler.
 “My Next Guest Needs No Introduction with David Letterman” brings Letterman back to hosting, following his 33-year career in late night television. The series has received eight Emmy nominations in its six seasons and won for Outstanding Hosted Nonfiction Series or Special in 2024. 
 The series is produced by Jax Media/Imagine Entertainment and Worldwide Pants, Inc. Executive producers are Tom Keaney and Mary Barclay for Worldwide Pants and Justin Wilkes, Michael Steed, Isabel Richardson and Yolanda T. Cochran for Jax Media/Imagine Entertainment. Producers are Tommy Alter, John Nemeth, Hunter Speese and Adam Donnelly for Jax Media/Imagine Entertainment.
 Watch the trailer for “My Next Guest Needs No Introduction with David Letterman” Season 7 below.
 *
 Michael Paré (“Eddie and the Cruisers,” “Streets of Fire”) is making his vertical microseries debut in the vertTV thriller “The Squatter Hunter,” which premieres Tuesday on the vertTV app.
 Paré plays an ex-military operative hired off the books to help a grieving daughter (Chelsea Rose Cook) reclaim her childhood home from a hostile squatter (Shayne Davis) after police are unable to intervene in the civil dispute, escalating the standoff into a life-or-death showdown.
 Alongside Paré, the series stars Savoy Bailey, Diane Robin and Demetris Owens and reunites “90210” stars Tori Spelling and Brian Austin Green. It is directed by David DeCoteau from a script by Adam Rockoff.
 Watch the full trailer below:
 *
 Happy holidays from the Griffin family!
 The long-running animated sitcom “Family Guy” is celebrating with a Hulu exclusive holiday special which premieres on Nov. 30 on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ for bundle subscribers in the U.S., and will exclusively stream internationally on Disney+ in most markets.
 The synopsis for the episode, titled “The Peter Cause,” reads: “It’s Christmas in Quahog, and Peter and the guys compete to become the town’s official Santa. Peter loses, and he can either process his disappointment in a mature manner, or give fans a memorable episode of ‘Family Guy.’ Thankfully, he chooses option number two.”
 Watch the trailer for the special below:
 Programming 
 The CW Network set 2027 midseason premiere dates for “Wild Cards,” “Penn & Teller: Fool Us,” “Masters of Illusion,” “Scrabble” and “Police 24/7.”
 The crime-solving procedural “Wild Cards” returns on Feb. 1, 2027. The 10-episode fourth season features returning cast members kicks Giacomo Gianniotti, Vanessa Morgan, Jason Priestley and Tamara Taylor.
 “Penn & Teller: Fool Us” and “Masters of Illusion” return on Jan. 22, 2027. Penn & Teller invite aspiring magicians to fool the world-famous duo with their best tricks. “Masters of Illusion” features performances from illusionists, escape artists and performers.
 “Scrabble” returns for its third season on Feb. 18, 2027. Hosted by Craig Ferguson, the show features contestants competing in word-based games for the ultimate $10,000 prize.
 “Police 24/7” returns with new episodes on March 10, 2027. From drug busts to routine traffic stops, the unscripted series gives unfiltered access to police departments across the U.S.

 NBC has unveiled its holiday programming, which includes the 100th anniversary of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.
 Annual programs returning to the network include “Christmas in Rockefeller Center,” the 25 th anniversary of “National Dog Show Presented by Purina” and new specials, including “Christmas with Snoop,” “America’s Parade: 100 Years of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade” and “Alan Jackson: The Last Show.”
 To celebrate 100 years, NBC will also air “NBC100: The Live Celebration,” a three-hour special recognizing the past century of stand-out moments. Additional star-studded events set for this holiday season include “Christmas at Graceland,” “94th Annual Christmas in Rockefeller Center,” “Dolly Parton’s Mountain Magic Christmas” and “A Toast to 2026!”
 NBC will also air holiday classics such as “How the Grinch Stole Christmas,” “Frosty the Snowman,” “Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer” and “It’s a Wonderful Life,” as well as the “Shrek” Christmas special, “Shrek the Halls.”
 *
 Tis the season to light the Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree! The two-hour “Christmas in Rockefeller Center” special will air live on Dec. 2 at 8 p.m. ET on NBC and simulcast on Peacock.
 Cynthia Erivo will make her hosting debut and perform during the live tree lighting special. The Emmy, Tony and Grammy Award winner will be joined by Kelly Clarkson, EJAE, Kirk Franklin, Wynonna Judd, JYT, Alanis Morissette, Brad Paisley, Alex Warren and more. The Radio City Rockettes will continue their holiday performance tradition. “TODAY” anchors Carson Daly, Craig Melvin and Al Roker will also be part of the celebration.
 “’Christmas in Rockefeller Center’ captures the spirit and magic of the holiday season, bringing together unforgettable performances, the energy of New York and a timeless tradition that connects generations,” said Jen Neal, Executive Vice President, Live Events and Specials, NBC & Peacock. “It’s incredibly special that we get to bring this moment to life year after year and share the excitement with millions of viewers.”
 “Christmas in Rockefeller Center” is produced by Universal Television in association with Jesse Collins Entertainment. Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay executive produce, with Glenn Weiss as director.
 An additional live hour of the special will be broadcast on NBC stations and some nationwide affiliates at 7 p.m. ET. Telemundo’s simulcast of “Navidades en Rockefeller Center (Christmas in Rockefeller Center)” will air live at 9 p.m. ET. “Christmas with Snoop” will follow the special, airing at 10 p.m. ET on NBC and next day on Peacock.
 *
 Dhar Mann Studios, Fox Entertainment and Holywater Tech announced the first five original scripted vertical dramas from their multi-year partnership.
 The five series will debut on Holywater Tech’s My Drama platform, beginning Nov. 25 and rolling out weekly through Dec. 22. The series feature storylines ranging from complicated relationships and family drama to dangerous secrets and unexpected second changes. The slate was developed specifically for vertical viewing.
 “When viewers ask you to make something, you want to get it right for them. Our audience is already watching vertical dramas, and they’ve asked us to join them there,” said Erin McFarlane, Dhar Mann Studios’ head of film and TV. “We’ve taken that to heart. We want these shows to have the romance, suspense and surprises they enjoy, and to give them that connection they feel with a Dhar Mann story—seeing a little of themselves in someone and really wanting things to work out for them.”
 The 40-title slate was announced in January. It marks Dhar Mann Studios’ first major expansion into vertical dramas with Holywater Tech’s mobile-first platform, with FOX Entertainment Global’s distribution.
 The five series and their release dates are below. Subscribers can access each title a week earlier.
“The Brothers Who Love Me” — Nov. 25
“Rescue Mission” — Dec. 1
“Married to the Wind” — Dec. 8
“Rhythm of the Heart” — Dec. 15
“The Rockstar Who Wants Me” — Dec. 22
 Events 
 “The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power” will take over The Orpheum Theatre & Club in downtown Los Angeles on Nov. 23.
 The fan activation will run from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. PT to celebrate the seventh episode of the show’s third season. The series is building toward one of the most iconic Middle-earth moments: the forging of the One Ring.
 Fans will step into the fiery world of Mount Doom inside The Orpheum Club. At the heart of “The Forge Experience” lies a photo moment for guests to raise the hammer to forge the One Ring. Beyond the forge, fans can see authentic series props, including the Rings of Power.
 Following the daytime activation, Prime Video partnered with Cinespia to host a special evening screening of “The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power” Season 3, Episode 7 inside the historic Orpheum Theatre from 7:30 to 9 p.m. PT. Screening attendees will be able to visit The Forge Experience at 6 p.m. when doors open for the showing. The evening will feature a live special guest musical performance, the episode screening and a post-screening panel discussion and Q&A with the series showrunners and creative talent.
 The first four episodes of Season 3 are available to stream now on Prime Video. Two new episodes premiere Nov. 18, with the final two episodes debuting Nov. 25.
 Executive News 
 Vice Studios announced three new executive appointments: Marcus Bullen, Uri Fleming and Jeff Boone.
 Marcus Bullen will be head of business development, Uri Fleming will be senior vice president, head of legal and business for North America and Jeff Boone will be vice president of scripted.
 As head of business development, Bullen will lead co-production partnerships and content financing deals to support the studio’s growth. He reports to president Amy Powell. Bullen comes from five years in content investment strategy at Disney’s streaming division and previously worked in financial restructuring at Houlihan Lokey across the US and UK markets.
 As senior vice president, head of legal and business affairs, North America, Fleming will report to global head of business affairs Paul Randle and will lead negotiations across development, production and distribution. He is the former head of global business affairs for unscripted television and original sports programming at Amazon MGM Studios. A former partner at Kleinberg, Lange, Cuddy & Carlo, Fleming began his career at Irell & Manella after earning a J.D. from USC Gould School of Law.
 As vice president of scripted, Boone will oversee domestic and international scripted projects. He reports to Adam Kassan, executive vice president of scripted film and television.
 Initiatives 
 Applications are now open for the Television Academy Foundation’s 2027 summer internship program.
 The program runs for eight weeks in Los Angeles and offers over 40 paid internships at top Hollywood production companies and studios to media arts college students. Undergraduate and graduate students enrolled in accredited colleges and universities, as well as students graduating in spring 2027, are eligible.
 “The Internship Program opens doors for aspiring television professionals, giving students invaluable opportunities to learn from industry leaders, develop their skills and build connections that can shape their careers,” said Tina Perry, chair of the Television Academy Foundation. “We’re proud to help emerging talent turn their passion for television into meaningful professional opportunities.”
 Participants get firsthand experience at leading studios and production facilities, across disciplines including animation, cinematography, development, directing, editing, production, news and writing.
 The Foundation offers internships for students interested in nonfiction television careers who attend college in Southern California, the Central Valley or a semester in LA program. Internships for foster youth in the Greater Los Angeles area are available with support from the Wolf Family Foundation.
 Students selected for the 2027 summer internship program will have the opportunity to participate in the Bob Bennett Future Leaders program, which grants selected interns a one-year student membership to the Television Academy and access to its alumni network.
 Applications are open until Jan. 13, 2027, at 5 p.m. PT. Finalists are selected by voting members of the Television Academy, with final selections made by participating host companies.
 Partnerships 
 “Icons Unearthed” will bring four standalone documentary titles to the Radial Original lineup, along with the company’s first factual pop-culture series, under Radial Entertainment’s new deal with The Nacelle Company.
 “Icons Unearthed” covers four standalone subtitles: “Transformers,” “Harrison Ford Movies,” “Arnold Schwarzenegger Movies” and “Quentin Tarantino Movies.” Each comprises six new hour-long episodes, with 24 total episodes across the slate to be released as standalones, rather than one collective season.
 The “Transformers” title follows Hasbro’s search for a hit toy line, Marvel Comics collaboration, Michael Bay’s blockbuster films and the big-screen reinvention. It will feature Glenn Morshower.
 The Harrison Ford title will explore his work with George Lucas and titles including “Blade Runner,” “Patriot Games,” “Clear and Present Danger” and “Air Force One.” It will feature Alison Doody.
 The Schwarzenegger title will follow his journey from bodybuilding to Hollywood, through his breakthrough roles and projects like “Twins” and “True Lies.” It will feature Jesse Ventura.
 The Tarantino title will look at the filmmaker’s rise from video-store clerk to Hollywood auteur, spanning his career through films like “Reservoir Dogs,” “Pulp Fiction,” “True Romance / NBK / From Dusk Till Dawn,” “Kill Bill,” “Inglourious Basterds” and “Django Unchained.” It will feature Bronson Pinchot.
